general.summary: Japan likely spent around $53 billion intervening in the currency market on Thursday in its ongoing struggle to prop up the yen, according to a Bloomberg analysis of central bank accounts.

general.title: Coinbase shares fall after crypto exchange posts disappointing second-quarter results
general.summary: Coinbase's Thursday report marked its third straight quarter missing Wall Street's forecasts for revenue and earnings.

general.title: Goldman Sees More South Africa Rating Upgrades on Strong Revenue
general.summary: South Africa’s revenue outperformance puts the country on course for further credit-ratings upgrades over the next year, Goldman Sachs Group Inc. said.

general.title: Euro-Area Inflation Strengthens as US-Iran Strikes Boost Oil
general.summary: Euro-area inflation picked up in July after the collapse of a US-Iran ceasefire boosted oil prices, reinforcing expectations that the European Central Bank will need to raise interest rates again.

general.title: China’s MiniMax and ByteDance Release Dueling AI Video Models
general.summary: MiniMax Group Inc. and ByteDance Ltd. released updates to their dueling AI video generation models within hours of each other, underscoring the aggressive advances that have made China the leader over the US in the burgeoning arena.

general.title: Colombia to Hike Interest Rate in Last Petro-Era Meeting
general.summary: Colombia’s central bank will likely lift its interest rate for the second straight month as inflation accelerates at the end of President Gustavo Petro’s term, which featured constant tension with the monetary authority.

general.title: Hong Kong’s Economy Slows More Than Forecast Despite AI Boom
general.summary: Hong Kong’s economic growth slowed more than forecast last quarter, even as a global rush to invest in artificial intelligence turbocharges the city’s exports.

general.title: European Execs Show AI Optimism: Markets Snapshot
general.summary: A big week of earnings results for some of the world's most influential companies has been underscored by the global AI infrastructure buildout, tightening supply chains and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty. The Opening Trade spoke to CEOs and corporate heavy weights to get clarity on their second-half outlook and whether they remain optimistic on returns from their AI investments. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Taiwan’s Economy Clocks Fastest First-Half Growth Since 1976
general.summary: Taiwan’s economy expanded at the fastest pace in some 50 years in the first half of 2026, data that should ease some concern among global investors about the outlook for AI.

general.title: Apple Leads Phone Revenues and Prices Up, Counterpoint Says
general.summary: Apple Inc. led a 7% increase in global smartphone revenue over the June quarter, showing how rising prices are offsetting shrinking shipments, according to Counterpoint Research.

general.title: SK Hynix, Samsung shares skyrocket to clock best days as AI rally roars back
general.summary: South Korea's chip heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics soared more than 20% on Friday, tracking a sharp rally in U.S. technology stocks.

general.title: European Stocks Trim Monthly Gain as Novo Nordisk and UMG Slump
general.summary: European shares pared some of their Friday gains as a decline on Novo Nordisk A/S weighed on the market, countering a rally in tech stocks and another round of largely upbeat results.

general.title: French Inflation Unexpectedly Accelerates on Services, Power
general.summary: French inflation unexpectedly quickened this month, supporting the case for another European Central Bank interest-rate increase.

general.title: Kioxia’s Outlook Miss Clouds Optimism About Memory Chip Boom
general.summary: Kioxia Holdings Corp. issued a disappointing earnings outlook after results missed expectations, a sign that an unprecedented AI-driven surge in flash memory prices may be moderating.

general.title: UK House Prices Edge Higher in July, Nationwide Says
general.summary: UK house prices returned to growth in July, one of the country’s largest mortgage lenders said, as buyers weather higher borrowing costs linked to the Iran war better than expected.
